title: gateway: REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE network blips escalate the whole daemon within seconds
description: Live (Mike's machine, 2026-08-31 05:06Z): a few-second network blip made dialer/anti-entropy/registry loops each exit REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE; supervisor restart backoff starts sub-second so the registry slot hit MAX_RESTARTS=5 within 4s -> escalation -> daemon exit. launchd KeepAlive recovered it in 6s, but joiners without a service (John) just drop off. Fix (same class as a2a-hak): treat REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE inside the registry/dialer/anti-entropy loops as a retryable poll failure — log once per state change, back off inside the loop (jittered, capped), keep the slot running, surface registry_error in health; reserve loop exit + supervisor escalation for non-network errors/panics. Also consider a supervisor minimum restart backoff (>=5s) so 5 restarts cannot fit in the 60s window on transient faults.
acceptance_criteria: with the registry unreachable for 60s+, all loops stay running (0 restarts), health shows registry_error, and normal operation resumes on recovery; no escalation
notes: SHIPPED 38e76ea: in-loop registry retry all three loops, health registry_error, live fault drill green (0 restarts through hard fault + recovery). 938/0.

title: fleet init clobbers joiner fleet identity — must refuse without --force
description: Live fleet incident (John): joiner machine had root.pub (ours) + gw.token, no root.key. He ran a2a mesh fleet init (likely following the GATEWAY_NOT_ENROLLED remedy text which names it) -> minted a NEW root + fleet-91322622, OVERWROTE root.pub, daemon then published under the wrong fleet with a token from the right one; peer looked healthy locally, invisible to the real fleet. Fix: fleet init refuses when mesh/fleet contains root.pub without root.key (joiner) or any existing root.key with different identity, unless --force; remedy text for GATEWAY_NOT_ENROLLED should not point joiners at fleet init (point at install-token/mesh-join doc). Also: daemon startup should VERIFY gw.token against root.pub and fail loud on mismatch instead of running split-brain.
acceptance_criteria: fleet init on a joiner home errors FLEET_ALREADY_JOINED with remedy; --force documented; startup token-vs-root verification fails loud; tests cover both

TRIGGER CORRECTED: John never ran fleet init — fleet LS did it. MeshFleetCmd::Ls and ::Revoke resolve fleet id via fleet_init(home) (mesh_cmd.rs:452,468) which MINTS when root.key is absent. Every read-only fleet command forks a joiner off its fleet. keys::fleet_id (safe reader, root.key-else-root.pub) already exists and is what the daemon uses. Escalating: fixing read paths inline now.
MINTING HALF FIXED + pushed (2df05f3): fleet_init joiner guard (FLEET_ALREADY_JOINED), Ls/Revoke on pure fleet_id reader, remedy text corrected, 3 regression tests, suite 918/0. REMAINING in this issue: daemon startup verification of gw.token against root.pub (fail loud on fleet mismatch instead of running split-brain).

title: Agent mesh: any-to-any agent communication, buzz feed, public endpoint registry
description:
Expand a2a beyond claude→codex dispatch into a full agent mesh, in two layers.

LAYER 1 — internal any-to-any: every local agent (claude sessions, codex workers) can discover each other, announce what it is working on, and push relevant context to another agent. Directions: claude↔claude, codex↔codex, codex→claude (claude→codex already exists via a2a spawn/send). Likely rides the existing a2a broker + file layer (owner registry, outbox/inbox) — brainstorm first.

LAYER 2 — 'slack for agents' (buzz-style, API-level): agents publish status/updates to a feed other agents subscribe to; direct fill-ins between agents over an agent-to-agent protocol. Transport: whatever is most efficient (HTTP/WebSocket first candidates; TCP/UDP if warranted). Public exposure via ngrok (or similar) hole-punch. Discovery via a public agent endpoint registry — centralized or decentralized; candidate backends: redis cluster or Neon postgres. Registry records per endpoint: owner, endpoint URL, created_at, actively-working flag, staleness since last update.

Workflow: superpowers:brainstorming first, then spec, then devloop plans — same lifecycle as a2a phases 1-5. Origin: Mike, 2026-08-20.
notes: ALL FOUR CHILDREN CLOSED. Layer 1 (internal mesh) shipped 2026-08-24; Layer 2 (fleet gateways + Neon registry) shipped 2026-08-26 — 11 tasks, all codex-built, 880 tests, real-socket loopback fleet e2e green. Recorded deferrals = the public door (stranger registration, trust tiers), e2e payload crypto, federation. Human-gated remaining: Neon connection string → fleet init + gated live tier; second-machine enrollment. Epic scope as filed is delivered.

title: broker: turn liveness watchdog — hung codex turns burn the full hour budget
description: Three occurrences (L1 T2, train car 1, L3 T2): codex app-server turn starts then emits ZERO events until the 1h timeout. A turn with no events for N minutes (config, default ~10m) is dead — the broker should fail it early (failed{turn_stalled}, respawnable) instead of waiting the full budget. Saves ~50min per occurrence on autonomous trains.

title: public hardening: worker FS read confinement + result-diff review gate for handoff
description: L3 v1 trust assumption (§1.1): an approved malicious brief can copy any worker-readable file into the checkout and the result push exfiltrates it. Hardening: confine worker filesystem reads to the checkout (codex sandbox policy), and/or a diff review gate (approver sees the result diff before push). Belongs to the public-hardening spec.

title: public hardening: registry write authorization (rows are peer-writable)
description: Found by the L3 spec review panel: every enrolled peer holds the registry DB credential and mesh_gateways rows are unconditional upserts keyed only by (fleet_id, gateway_id) — any peer can rewrite another gateway's cert_fpr/pubkey_fpr/endpoint_url (MITM-in-fleet, impersonation). L3 routes around it (never authorizes from the registry). Hardening: per-row ownership proofs (signed upserts verified by a trigger/function), or per-gateway DB roles / RLS, or a registry gateway service. Belongs to the public-hardening spec.

title: gateway registry slot: exposure failure must degrade, not kill heartbeats
description: Live fleet observation (John's machine): daemon running but ngrok agent down -> exposure.current_url() errors on every tick -> registry slot exits -> supervisor restart with compounding jittered backoff (cap 1920s) -> ZERO registry heartbeats for 12+ min, row goes stale, peer looks dead while the daemon reports healthy. Fix: on exposure error, heartbeat the registry anyway with endpoint_url=None (row degrades to undialable but stays live/fresh), log the exposure error, keep the slot running. Backoff only the exposure retry, not the heartbeat.
notes: SHIPPED 982240c: degrade-not-die verified LIVE (ngrok killed: heartbeats stayed fresh, endpoint preserved, 0 restarts; recovery republished). 927/0.

title: dialer: reset backoff when a peer's registry row changes
description: Dial failures compound toward outbound_retry_max_secs (1920s). When a peer's endpoint_url or cert_fpr CHANGES in the registry, that is new information — clear next_dial_after/attempts for that peer so recovery is immediate instead of waiting out the old cooldown. Observed live: peer registered mid-backoff and stayed unlinked ~30min until daemon restart.
notes: SHIPPED 8988a01 (train car 5).
